title: How do I transfer issuer-sponsored shares (SRN) to my margin loan?
answer: Use the Security Transfer Form (LE044) to lodge issuer-sponsored shares held under an SRN to your Margin Loan.
steps: Section 1 (Facility Details): enter your Loan Account Name and Loan Account Number.
Section 2 (Equity Instructions): tick 'Lodge equities (shares) to the Margin Loan'.

Section 3 (Lodgement Instructions): enter your Margin Loan HIN and registered name, then tick 'Lodge Issuer Sponsored security to the Margin Loan Facility' and list the security code, SRN and number of shares.
Attach your latest issuer-sponsored holding statement for each security.
Section 5: every security owner signs and dates the form. Companies and trusts indicate the signing capacity.
Send it by mail to Leveraged, GPO Box 5388, Sydney NSW 2001, or email customerservice@leveraged.com.au.
notes: If the shares are not held in the Borrower's or a Guarantor's name, you also need an original Australian Standard Transfer Form to change ownership.
A fee may be payable when a transfer results in a change of ownership. See the fee schedule.

title: How do I transfer money into my margin loan?
answer: You can put money into your Loan Account by bank transfer (EFT), BPAY or direct debit from your nominated bank account. Money you deposit reduces your loan balance.
steps: Find your payment details: log in to Leveraged Online and go to Profile and settings > Facility details. They're also in your welcome letter.
EFT: transfer to your Loan Account's BSB and account number (an Adelaide Bank account used only for payments into your Loan Account).
BPAY: pay using the BPAY details for your Loan Account.
Direct debit: ask us to debit your nominated bank account. Direct debits take three business days to clear, so a debit processed on Monday is available Thursday morning.
Check the deposit has arrived by logging in to Leveraged Online.
notes: Use EFT or BPAY rather than posting a cheque, to avoid delays.

Not sure your details are right? Call 1300 307 807 (Mon–Fri, 8:30am–5:30pm AEST/AEDT) to confirm them, or email customerservice@leveraged.com.au. Never send money to account details received in an unexpected email or call.
To nominate or change a bank account for direct debits, we need confirmation of the BSB, account number and account name from your bank, usually a bank statement.

title: How do I transfer broker-sponsored shares (HIN) to my margin loan?
answer: Use the Security Transfer Form (LE044). You can lodge a whole broker-sponsored HIN, or selected securities from it.
steps: Section 1: enter your Loan Account Name and Loan Account Number.
Section 2: tick 'Lodge equities (shares) to the Margin Loan'.
Section 3: enter your Margin Loan HIN and registered name, then choose one option:

Option A: 'Lodge following broker sponsored HIN'. This moves every holding in that HIN and keeps your existing TFN and dividend instructions. Enter the broker name, broker account number and broker HIN.
Option B: 'Transfer the following Broker Sponsored security'. List the broker details, security code and number of shares. You may need to re-nominate TFN and dividend instructions.
Section 5: every security owner signs and dates the form.
Send it by mail to Leveraged, GPO Box 5388, Sydney NSW 2001, or email customerservice@leveraged.com.au.
notes: If the shares are not held in the Borrower's or a Guarantor's name, you also need an original Australian Standard Transfer Form.

title: How do I release shares from my margin loan?
answer: Use the Security Transfer Form (LE044), section 4 'Release Equity from the Margin Loan'.
steps: Section 1: enter your Loan Account Name and Loan Account Number.
Section 2: tick 'Release equities from the Margin Loan'.

Section 4: enter the Margin Loan HIN and registered name, then choose to release the whole broker-sponsored HIN, all holdings to a broker-sponsored account, selected securities to broker-sponsored, or a security to issuer-sponsored (with its SRN).
Section 5: every security owner signs and dates the form.
Send it by mail or email to Leveraged.
notes: Releasing shares reduces the security behind your loan. Check your available funds and loan-to-value position first.

title: How do I apply for a loan?
answer: Most people apply online in one sitting. Read the PDS for the product first. You can also talk to a Business Development Manager before you start.
steps: Compare the Margin Loan, Investment Funds Multiplier and Direct Investment Loan.
Read the PDS and Product Guide for the loan you choose.
Complete the online application.
notes: The Direct Investment Loan is available to individual and joint borrowers only, not companies or trusts.
Leveraged loans are not available to self-managed superannuation funds.

title: Who can apply for the Direct Investment Loan?
answer: The Direct Investment Loan is available to individual and joint borrowers only. It is not available to companies, trusts or self-managed superannuation funds. Managed funds are not acceptable investments for this loan, and the maximum credit limit is $500,000.

title: What are your current interest rates?
answer: As at 07/10/2026 the standard variable rates are: Direct Investment Loan 8.59% p.a., Margin Loan 10.95% p.a., Investment Funds Multiplier 10.95% p.a. Fixed rates and Rewards Plus rates are on the rates page. Wholesale rates are available for eligible clients with facilities over $500,000. Contact your Business Development Manager to discuss them.
notes: Rates are indicative and subject to change. The rate on your loan may be different.

title: Who can I talk to about opening a new facility?
answer: For new direct clients, talk to Young Ngai, Business Development Manager for direct clients, on 03 8633 1236. Financial advisers can find their regional BDM on the Adviser-only page. For existing accounts, call 1300 307 807, Monday to Friday, 8:30am to 5:30pm AEST/AEDT.

title: What can I borrow against?
answer: Each loan has its own acceptable investments list showing the eligible securities and their lending ratios. Check the recent changes list too. Lists can change at any time.

title: What is a margin call and what do I need to do?
answer: A margin call is made when your loan balance goes above your lending value plus the buffer. This usually happens when the market value of your investments falls, which lowers your lending value.
steps: If you get a margin call you'll usually need to act within 24 hours.
Reduce the shortfall by repaying some of the loan, adding cash or acceptable investments, or selling investments.
If you don't act, Leveraged can sell investments for you.
notes: Between your lending value and the buffer limit you can't draw more funds, but no margin call is made.
Keep your margin call contact details up to date so we can reach you quickly.

title: How are lending value, available funds and margin calls worked out?
answer: Lending value is each holding's market value multiplied by its lending ratio, added up. Available funds are the lower of your lending value and credit limit, minus your loan balance. The 'How it works' page has worked examples and a calculator.

title: What fees do you charge?
answer: There's no establishment fee for individual Margin Loan borrowers, and no fee for adding Exchange Options Plus, Instalment Plus or Rewards Plus. Paying money into your loan is free. Some fees apply in specific situations.
steps: Companies: $150 establishment fee. Trusts: $250 to review the trust deed if you don't provide a solicitor's trust opinion (refunded if the application is declined).
Same-day (TT/RTGS) payment out of your loan: $26. Standard payments out: free.
Dishonours: $35 for a failed direct debit, $9 for a failed transfer from your loan account.
Breaking a fixed rate: break costs apply, minimum $250.
Other fees, such as off-market transfers ($25 per security) and late settlement ($30 per contract note), are in the fee schedule.
notes: Fees differ between products. Check the fee schedule for the Investment Funds Multiplier and Direct Investment Loan.

title: What happens to a margin loan when someone dies?
answer: We're sorry for your loss. Please let us know as soon as you can, so we can suspend the account and stop any further debits or fees.
steps: Call 1300 307 807 (Mon–Fri, 8:30am–5:30pm AEST/AEDT, or +61 2 8282 8282 from overseas) or email customerservice@leveraged.com.au.
Give us their full name, loan account number (if known), residential and mailing address, date of birth and date of passing.
We'll check all their accounts with us, suspend the facility and write to the personal representatives or solicitor with what's needed to settle the estate.
You may be asked for certified copies of the death certificate and grant of probate or letters of administration, ID for the executor, and signed instructions for the loan.

title: Can an SMSF get a margin loan?
answer: No. Our margin loans, the Direct Investment Loan and the add-on features aren't available to self-managed superannuation funds (SMSFs).

title: What's the difference between your loans?
answer: We offer three loans. The Margin Loan is the most flexible: borrow against shares, ETFs and managed funds. The Investment Funds Multiplier is for building a managed-fund portfolio with regular contributions. The Direct Investment Loan is a structured loan for direct shares and ETFs with no margin calls; it's for individuals and joint borrowers only.

title: Is there a minimum loan amount?
answer: We don't publish a minimum loan amount for the Margin Loan, Investment Funds Multiplier or Direct Investment Loan, so please call us to check. If you use Instalment Plus for regular investing, the minimums are $1,000 of your own money and a $2,000 loan drawdown to start, then $250 a month from you and $250 a month borrowed.

title: What is Instalment Plus?
answer: Instalment Plus is a free add-on for the Margin Loan and Investment Funds Multiplier. Each month it invests some of your own money plus a matching loan drawdown, so you progressively build a managed funds portfolio.
steps: Minimums to start: $1,000 of your own money and a $2,000 loan drawdown.
Then each month: at least $250 of your own money and $250 borrowed ($500 a month added to your portfolio).
New customers: choose it in your margin loan application. Existing customers: use the Instalment Plus Application and Maintenance form.
notes: Not available for self-managed superannuation funds.
Borrowing to invest magnifies gains and losses. Read the fact sheet and PDS before applying.

title: Can I borrow against property or REITs?
answer: We don't lend against direct property, such as a house, apartment or land, and our loans can't be used to buy one. You can borrow to invest in listed property trusts (REITs) that are on our acceptable investments lists, alongside shares, ETFs and managed funds.
notes: Each REIT has its own lending ratio. Check the latest acceptable investments list for your product.

title: What do I need for my tax return? Where is my end of financial year interest?
answer: Your end of financial year interest is on page 2 of your June statement. We report the interest on your loan only. We don't report on trades, capital gains or profit and loss, so get those from your broker.
steps: Open your June statement in Leveraged Online, or ask us for a copy.
Go to page 2 for the interest for the financial year.
For trades, capital gains and profit and loss, ask your broker or platform for their tax report.
notes: We can't give tax advice. Talk to your accountant or tax adviser about what you can claim.
